title: Function Library: String Tools
story: Every programmer eventually builds a personal library of utility functions — small, reusable tools that solve common problems. Today you'll craft five string utilities that you'll use over and over: counting characters, reversing text, detecting blanks, checking prefixes, and stripping spaces.
why: Building a library of focused string utilities teaches the pattern of small, composable functions where each tool solves exactly one well-defined problem.
analogy: Your string tool library is like a Swiss Army knife. The `count_char` blade counts how many times a letter appears. The `reverse` corkscrew flips text backwards. The `is_blank` magnifying glass inspects for emptiness. The `remove_spaces` scissors trim out gaps. Each tool is simple on its own, but carrying all five gives you a complete text-manipulation kit.
try_it: Add two more tools to your library: `count_words_starting_with(text: Str, ch: Char) -> Int` that counts how many words begin with a given character, and `replace_char(text: Str, old: Char, new: Char) -> Str` that replaces every occurrence of one character with another.
tips: reverse builds the result backwards — start i at len-1 and decrement
is_blank is true for both empty strings and strings containing only spaces
starts_with_hello checks length first — a 3-character string can't start with 'Hello'
remove_spaces is a filter: copy characters to result only if they're not spaces
common_mistakes: In reverse, starting i at len instead of len-1 — strings are 0-indexed
In is_blank, returning false on first non-space but forgetting to return true after the loop
In starts_with_hello, accessing indices beyond the string length — always check len >= 5 first
Using string concatenation inside loops without string.str_concat — may not work as expected
